# Pokémon Survivors

> A free, unofficial Vampire Survivors-style Pokémon fan game (action roguelite / bullet heaven) that runs in the browser and on phones, with no download, no ads and no purchases (and no sign-up to play solo). Play solo or in online co-op for up to 4 players. Available in English, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, French and Traditional Chinese. Made by Pedro Barretto; open source on GitHub.

Pick one of 27 starter Pokémon from every region (Kanto to Paldea), walk around and let it attack on its own. Survive 15 minutes of wild Pokémon hordes, collect experience, learn moves, equip held items and evolve mid-run, then face Mewtwo. After the victory you can keep going in an endless mode, where the horde keeps scaling and Arceus hunts you as the reaper. Beat the legendaries as bosses to catch them, then play as any of the 23 in Legend Mode. Or create a room and play online co-op with up to 3 friends.

- 27 starters, each with its full 3-stage evolution line, stats, signature move and learnset
- Online co-op for 2 to 4 players: one player creates a room and invites friends with the room link, its 5-character code or the friends list (which shows who is online, in a room or playing). Everyone plays their own Pokémon in the same run; EXP is shared (the whole team levels up on the same beat and picks at once), the horde, bosses and Poké Dollars scale with the team, the ₽ is split among the players, and each player gets their own TMs, Poké Balls, Alpha prizes and Mega Stones. A fainted player lies as a Poké Ball until a teammate stands by them; the run ends when nobody can carry on, and a dropped connection reconnects into the same run. It needs an account with a @handle. For now co-op plays the standard mode: places, landmarks and rift domains (rift legendaries fight in an arena), Legend Mode, shop items (Bag, TMs, evolution items, Bottle Caps), the daily outbreak, Halloween Night, the Daily Challenge and the rankings stay in solo runs
- Eggs: bosses, locked chests and rifts sometimes drop an egg; it waits in a 3-slot incubator (the Kecleon Shop sells a 4th and a 5th slot for good, and the Quick Incubator, which makes one egg walk twice as fast) and hatches with the steps walked in runs, unlocking one of 54 more playable families (every type and generation, e.g. Pichu, Eevee, Gastly, Magikarp, Riolu, Gible, Bagon, Deino, Dreepy). 1% of hatchlings are shiny for good; duplicates become Poké Dollars. A 55th family, Munchlax → Snorlax, only hatches from the Friendship Egg, and four ghost families (Litwick → Lampent → Chandelure, Phantump → Trevenant, Drifloon → Drifblim, Sandygast → Palossand) only from the Haunted Egg, which Duskull's stall sells on the plaza during Halloween Night (₽6,000 or 1,000 candies, as many as the incubator holds, 25% each; back next year), and four more (Porygon → Porygon2 → Porygon-Z, Exeggcute → Exeggutor, Scraggy → Scrafty, and Smeargle, which never evolves and copies foes' moves with Sketch) only from the Kecleon Egg, the Showcase's fixed card (₽10,000 for the day's first, each one after double the last, up to 6 a day per player, 25% each) (90 playable Pokémon in all)
- Invites and Mystery Gifts: every shared link carries the player's handle; a friend who signs up through it gets a Friendship Egg, and the inviter gets gifts once the friend has finished 3 runs (1 friend: a Friendship Egg; 3: the Ambassador title and an exclusive card frame; 5: an Ultra rare egg; 10: a shiny Dratini). The home screen's Invite friends card shows the link, the reward ladder and each invited friend's progress. Public profiles show how many friends a player brought
- 207 moves and 32 held items. Every family has its own signature move (Brave Bird, Weather Ball, Spore, Fiery Dance, Gigaton Hammer, Moonblast…) and a learnset that grows at each evolution, with more moves than the 6 slots, so runs build differently. A maxed regular move plus the right item evolves (Ember + Charcoal → Flamethrower; 48 move evolutions, 7 type items for Fighting, Steel, Ghost, Dark, Psychic, Ground and Fairy), and evolved moves keep leveling up to Lv 5
- Level-up choices: every base move forks into two paths at Lv 4 and Lv 7 that change how it plays (bounce, explode, trail, echo…); cards roll a rarity (rare: +2 levels; shiny, 1 in 64: a free pick); a Forget button bans an offer for the rest of the run (charges from the Escape Rope, bosses and evolutions); and each run opens with a draft for the 2nd move
- 91 Abilities, one picked out of 3 at the first evolution (the third is the Hidden Ability), and branching evolutions: Eevee picks among its 8 eeveelutions (the weather and place favor one), Kirlia picks Gardevoir or Gallade, and Snorunt, Poliwhirl, Scyther and Charcadet branch too, each form with its own type, special, moves and Abilities
- Moves from outside the learnset: every beaten wave boss drops a TM (Rock Slide, Yawn, Ice Beam, Discharge, Heat Wave, Psystrike…), a Move Tutor tent teaches moves that suit the player's type but sit outside its learnset, and each rift legendary or final mythical offers its own legendary move (Whirlwind, Sacred Fire, Origin Pulse, Roar of Time, Wish…; one per run). All 23 legendaries have one; the trios, Mewtwo and Arceus use theirs only in Legend Mode and in their boss fights (Snowscape, Electric Terrain, Overheat, Thunderclap, Burning Bulwark, Aqua Ring, Rock Wrecker, Glaciate, Metal Burst, Telekinesis, Judgment). With 6 moves, learning asks which one to forget
- Duo moves: two maxed moves whose types form a recipe fuse into Fire Pledge, Water Pledge, Grass Pledge, Fusion Flare, Fusion Bolt, Ion Deluge, Freeze-Dry or Nightmare (one per run). Locked chests may hide a cursed item (Life Orb, Choice Band, Flame Orb, Iron Ball): strong, at a price, take it or leave it
- Type matchups, burn, poison, paralysis, slow, sleep, freeze, confusion, marks, Leech Seed-style seeds and weaken, and a manual special attack for each of the 18 types that grows stronger at the final evolution (Blast Burn, Hydro Cannon, Frenzy Plant, Bolt Strike, Draco Meteor, Astral Barrage, Precipice Blades, Aeroblast and more). Agile lines (Treecko, Sprigatito, Riolu, Gible, Starly, Honedge) get a chain dash instead: a lunge into the nearest foe that can jump again to the next one right after a hit; Aegislash gets Stance Change, swapping between Shield Forme (takes less damage) and Blade Forme (hits harder)
- 415 wild Pokémon from all 9 generations (Dragon types included), with every non-legendary Kanto, Johto and Hoenn species (but Unown and Castform), in 5 tiers by base stat total; every run draws its own cast (basic Pokémon early, evolved ones late), weighted towards the types of each biome
- Legendary bosses with telegraphed attacks: Onix, Snorlax, a legendary trio drawn per run for the 7:00, 9:30 and 12:00 slots (Kanto birds Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres; Johto beasts Raikou, Entei and Suicune; or Hoenn Regis Regirock, Regice and Registeel; each slot has the same stats whichever trio comes) and Mewtwo, sometimes joined by a rare mythical (Mew, Celebi or Jirachi, 10%). Each one switches between close and ranged attacks and enrages under half HP, the horde thins for the first minute of each boss, and each boss has until the next one arrives, then it flees; Mewtwo, the finale, blasts the horde away and thins it further while it stands. Bosses aim at the path the player is taking, leap at a player who keeps away, unlock a new attack when enraged and get an extra one on Nightmare. The legendaries on the map (the trio, the mythical, Mewtwo and Arceus) make an entrance (the birds swoop down, the beasts leap in, the Regis rise from the ground) with a title card and epithet (ZAPDOS · Lord of Thunder) and their own theme, and fight in 3 phases marked on the HP bar: the second brings a new way to move, the third an ultimate built on their legendary move, always with a marked safe spot (Arceus's Judgment takes the biome's type). When one falls, a quick Poké Ball capture plays on the map
- Elites and runners: when the horde nearly fills, new enemies come in as tougher elites (except during the Mewtwo duel), and one new species each stage runs and aims where the player is heading. Another species per stage spits: it keeps its distance and fires slow, telegraphed shots flavored by its type (fire, water, poison puddles, electric, grass) that pass through the player's aura
- Alpha Pokémon: from about 4:00, oversized red-glowing members of the stage's top tier join the horde; they ignore knockback and charge along a red lane they aim first (on Nightmare the charge ends in a shockwave and they enrage). Beating one gives EXP, ₽ and the Alpha's prize, a level-up of rare cards; the Alpha Hunter title comes with 100 of them
- Five biomes per run (Route 1, Viridian Forest, Mt. Moon, Mt. Silver, Lavender Tower), each with its own music, and weather that shifts type matchups for everyone: harsh sunlight, rain, sandstorm, snow and fog
- Special enemies with behavior traits, at most one per stage of a run: Chansey heals the horde, Bronzor and Bronzong shield it, Nidoqueen summons Nidoran, Voltorb, Electrode and Drifloon explode, Magnemite and Vikavolt fire telegraphed beams and Hitmonlee and Lokix leap over the horde
- Epic legendary rifts: two optional portals per run (around 4:00 and 10:20), and the run clock stops inside. An omen comes first: the legendary's weather takes the sky for 20 s, then a huge tear opens. Inside, each legendary has its own domain in 4 acts: a crossing bigger than the screen past its retinue with a threat pushing from behind (rising tide in the Seafloor Cavern for Kyogre, a lava wall in the Magma Cavern for Groudon, floors crumbling into the clouds on the Sky Pillar for Rayquaza, whirlpools and a storm surge on the Whirl Islands for Lugia, the burning Bell Tower for Ho-Oh, time stopping, skipping and rewinding on Spear Pillar for Dialga, a dream mist on Southern Island for Latias and Latios, who fight together, and the Drifting Meteoroid crumbling into the void for Deoxys); an encounter with a title card (KYOGRE · Lord of the Seas) and its own theme; a battle in 3 phases where each phase transforms the arena and builds to a telegraphed signature ultimate with a readable safe spot (Water Spout and Origin Pulse, Eruption and Precipice Blades, Dragon Ascent, Aeroblast and Sky Attack, Ho-Oh's rebirth and Burn Up, Roar of Time freezing your attacks mid-air, the Mist Ball and Luster Purge lattice, one Deoxys Forme per phase); and a Poké Ball capture scene. Legendaries may be shiny (1 in 8); fainting inside sends you back to the map with 30% HP instead of ending the run
- Places: a few times per run the entrance to a place shows up on the map (with an edge arrow); standing in its doorway steps in, the world outside waits, and each place has its own Pokémon, goal and time limit. Dark Cave: a Mystery Dungeon of dark floors (light around the player, wider for Fire and Electric types) with stairs, a Monster House and a treasure chest, and the PMD wind that blows you out. Haunted Graveyard: only ghosts, rising from the graves; their spirits wake Spiritomb out of the Odd Keystone (a boss, possibly shiny) before dawn. Above the Clouds: only for Flying types, who ride an updraft up where only flying Pokémon come and wings (Health, Muscle, Resist, Swift, Pretty) drift in on the wind, each raising a stat for the rest of the run
- Hidden zones: in about a third of runs, a secret entrance shows up with no arrow and no warning, dressed as scenery just ahead of the player (rustling leaves, a glinting cracked rock); walking up to it finds it. Hidden Grotto (Black 2/White 2): Audino, sometimes Chansey or Blissey, pop out of shaking grass, shy and worth a lot of EXP, plus an item in the grass. Underground (Diamond/Pearl): dig glints in the walls for Exp. Candy, spheres worth Poké Dollars, Rare Candy, a missing evolution stone or Old Amber with an egg, while each dig cracks the walls and Diglett pop out of holes. Each zone has a rare dweller found nowhere else (Shaymin, Diancie).
- Landmarks: points of interest placed on the map from the run's seed, dressed by each biome: an abandoned roofless cottage (walk in; a crate inside), a mine tunnel (stand in one mouth to come out of the other, under the ridge, while the horde loses track), a hedge maze with a chest at its heart, Unown ruins with an altar whose glyphs light up (Exp. Candy), and an abandoned camp with a backpack by the fire (Oran Berries). Each treasure opens once by standing at it; a sign names the landmark as the player comes close. Two achievements count the treasures opened. Bushes, fallen logs and lone rocks and trees are strewn between them.
- Mega Evolution: the first rift legendary beaten with a Mega line drops its Mega Stone; at the final evolution a MEGA button (E key, gamepad Y) Mega Evolves for 20 s with a 60 s recharge. 38 Megas across 33 lines, each with its own stats, special and ability: Mega Venusaur, Mega Charizard X (Dragon Flare, a blue dragon-fire dash) and Y (Drought: harsh sunlight), Mega Blastoise, Mega Raichu X and Y, Mega Alakazam (Trace: every special also fires two of your moves), Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag: foes nearby are slowed), Mega Dragonite, Mega Meganium, Mega Feraligatr, Mega Tyranitar (Sand Stream: a sandstorm it is immune to), Mega Sceptile, Mega Blaziken, Mega Swampert (Swift Swim: rain), Mega Gardevoir (Pixilate, Moonblast), Mega Gallade (Inner Focus: a 6-jump chain dash that bursts Aura Spheres), Mega Pidgeot (No Guard, Air Slash), Mega Gyarados, Mega Ampharos, Mega Scizor (Technician, Bullet Punch chain dash), Mega Houndoom, Mega Aggron (Filter), Mega Manectric (Intimidate: foes nearby are slowed), Mega Altaria (Pixilate), Mega Banette (Prankster), Mega Glalie (Refrigerate), Mega Salamence (Aerilate), Mega Metagross, Mega Staraptor, Mega Garchomp and Mega Garchomp Z, Mega Lucario (Adaptability, a 6-jump chain dash bursting Aura Spheres) and Mega Lucario Z, Mega Emboar, Mega Chesnaught, Mega Delphox and Mega Greninja. A line with two Megas gets both stones and keeps the one it picks up. In Legend Mode, Mega Latias, Mega Latios and Mega Mewtwo Y use the same button
- Endless mode after Mewtwo, scored by time survived, with Arceus as a hunting reaper that can be defeated
- Legend Mode: all 23 legendaries are playable (Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres, Raikou, Entei, Suicune, Regirock, Regice, Registeel, Mew, Celebi, Jirachi, Mewtwo, Lugia, Ho-Oh, Kyogre, Groudon, Rayquaza, Dialga, Latias, Latios, Deoxys, Arceus), each caught by beating it as a boss in any mode: 3 wins for rift and trio legendaries, 5 for Mewtwo, 1 for the mythicals Mew, Celebi and Jirachi, and Arceus only in endless mode once the other 22 are caught. Each escape shows the count (Kyogre broke free… 2/3); a shiny beaten on the catching win, or after, unlocks its shiny. Caught legendaries sit in the partner select's Legendaries tab. A legend never evolves: it awakens at Lv 12 and Lv 28 (Ability pick, stats, a Forget charge; the second turns Kyogre and Groudon Primal and Rayquaza Mega), opens with its legendary move, carries an innate Ability (Drizzle, Drought, Air Lock, Levitate, Serene Grace, Multitype…) and Deoxys swaps Formes with its special. Same run length and the same three difficulties, with a denser, tougher horde (Pressure); a legend never faces itself (a Mewtwo meets the Mewtwo Clone). Legend Mode runs have their own ranking board Event legend: on Halloween Night 2026 (October 24 to November 2, Brasília time), Darkrai is playable too. In a haunted run any rift can turn into its Nightmare rift; 2 wins catch it, and it plays with the legendary move Dark Void (orbs of darkness that put crowds to sleep) and the innate Bad Dreams (sleeping foes near it take damage without waking). Community goal: if every account's candy jar adds up to 15 million during the event (each trainer counting up to 20,000), Darkrai gets its Mega Evolution for everyone, for good: its second awakening, at Lv 28, turns it into Mega Darkrai, the form it also takes in its rift's last phase. The progress bar is on the in-game Halloween Night screen. It only shows up during the event, keeps the Halloween Night 2026 badge on the partner select, stays with whoever caught it, and does not count toward Arceus.
- Three difficulty levels, all open from the start: Normal, Hard (faster, denser hordes that hit harder) and Nightmare (brutal, fast and dense hordes and half of every heal). Standing still doesn't work: late hordes resist knockback and hit harder, armor takes off at most half of a hit, a hidden pressure director sends faster and closer spawns to a player who isn't getting hurt, and the map itself strikes where the player stands (Thunder in the rain, hail in the snow, Rock Slide in a sandstorm, Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes), always telegraphed on the ground
- Rankings by time survived, one per difficulty, for today, this week and all time (days and weeks follow Brasília time), filterable by starter and by friends (one-way follows), and a separate Legendary board (Standard | Legendary) for Legend Mode runs, also split by difficulty. Signed-in players get a public profile at /?u=handle with their title, records, Pokédex progress and recent runs. A ranked run shows on the boards as soon as it ends, within what a start token's wall clock allows; the server re-simulates the replays of the runs at the top (the simulation is deterministic across browsers) and takes off any that don't end where they said
- Shiny wild Pokémon and shiny starters; Poké Dollars and permanent upgrades in the Kecleon Shop (the Shiny Charm takes wild shiny odds from 1/450 to 1/225)
- Daily mass outbreak: one wild species per day (Brasília time), the same for everyone, is the most common Pokémon of every run that day, so its shiny shows up about twice a run; a daily mission asks to defeat it
- Daily Challenge: one run per day (Brasília time) that is the same for everyone, drawn from the date: seed, Pokémon (any playable one, egg families not yet hatched included, the Haunted and Kecleon Eggs' families aside) and difficulty, with no shop upgrades, Bag items or Shiny Charm, and the day's outbreak on. Only each player's first finished run counts on the challenge board (today and yesterday), the rest are practice; the server checks the run is the day's challenge and re-simulates it. After the day closes, everyone on the board gets a ribbon as a Mystery Gift (gold: top 10%, silver: top half, bronze: took part), shown on the public profile and the Trainer Card
- Kecleon Shop: a place in the lobby (a plaza east of the partner's home; walk there or press Shop) run by Kecleon, who greets you with lines that follow what you did (a first visit, a win against Mewtwo, a daily streak, your partner's type, a wishlist item back in stock). Shelves: today's Showcase (the same for everyone, turns over at midnight Brasília time: a free gift a day, the Kecleon Egg's fixed card (₽10,000, then each one double the last, ₽20k/40k/80k/160k/320k, up to 6 a day; outside the rotation and the deal; not sold while the incubator is full), a deal at 30% off, cards drawn from the consumables, the day's egg and a style, every item back within 7 days, a wishlist from the Tent on); the Bag (9 consumables, one of each per run, 2 to 4 different ones by shop level: Lure for twice the shinies, Incense for twice the eggs, Rare Candy to start at Lv 3, Lucky Egg +25% EXP, Luck Incense +50% Poké Dollars, Honey for twice the outbreak, X Attack +10% damage, Max Revive to get up once at half HP, Everstone for a run that never evolves at +15% to every stat; the ranking shows each run's items); TMs from Kecleon's purple brother (from the Tent; owned for good, 1 or 2 armed before a run become its first TM discs; the TMs a run taught are always listed, the others rotate 3 a day; 10 shop exclusives: Pay Day, Thief, Protect, Hyper Beam, Rain Dance and Sunny Day (they call their weather over the run's), Swords Dance, Drain Punch, Thunder Wave, Fly); Evolution items (from the Shop level; a branch that needs an item in the official games needs it in a run: Gallade and Froslass the Dawn Stone, Politoed the King's Rock, Scizor the Metal Coat, Kleavor the Black Augurite, Armarouge and Ceruledge their armors, Espeon, Umbreon, Leafeon, Glaceon and Sylveon their stones; Gardevoir, Glalie and Poliwrath stay free; without items Eevee evolves into Vaporeon, Jolteon or Flareon, drawn at random, and every stone held joins a choice; Scyther and Charcadet without an item don't evolve and get +15% to every stat; line steps can need one too: Porygon2 the Up-Grade, Porygon-Z the Dubious Disc, Exeggutor the Leaf Stone, and without it the form before stays at +15%; owned for good, or found in a run: a boss down has a 30% chance to drop a missing one, kept until the run ends); Training (the permanent upgrades, refundable, and Bottle Caps: +3% to every stat per level, 3 levels per Pokémon); Style (card frames, backgrounds, PC Box wallpapers); and Expansion (invest Poké Dollars to grow the shop through 5 levels, Cart, Tent, Shop, Kecleon Mart and Department Store, for ₽30k/100k/300k/800k: a bigger building on the plaza, more Showcase cards and Bag slots, Kecleon's purple brother, Meowth's caravan from the Kecleon Mart, the Tycoon title, the Golden Kecleon frame and a golden Kecleon statue at the Department Store). Meowth's caravan parks on the plaza Friday to Sunday (Brasília time) with a weekly stock: an ultra egg, the Gold Bottle Cap (one Pokémon straight to 3 Bottle Caps), the Meowth frame and two exclusive TMs, one of each per weekend; with 7 loyalty stamps he takes 20% off for the weekend. The loyalty card stamps each day you visit the shop (no purchase needed, missed days never reset): a rare egg at 7, the Regular frame at 14, the VIP Customer title at 30, the golden statue at 60, a Kecleon Egg sure to hatch shiny at 100. Seasonal stalls stand on the plaza during events (Duskull's on Halloween Night, which sells the Haunted Egg; Delibird's at Christmas). Some missions pay a Bag item
- Plaza Festival (Festival da Praça): about once a month, for 14 days, the fountain on the Kecleon plaza is a community Poké Dollar pot. Signed-in players with a @handle and 3 verified runs toss ₽ into it (whole amounts from ₽100, at most ₽200k per Brasília day, taken by the server from the synced save); every milestone the pot reaches is a Mystery Gift for every player, guests and non-donors included, claimable until 7 days after the end. Giving ₽50k in one festival earns the Patron (Mecenas) title, and the top 10 donors by @handle are listed on the fountain's plaque (a player can hide their name). The first, the Lantern Festival (Festival das Lanternas), runs Nov 3 to 16, 2026: ₽10M a Rare Egg, ₽30M the Lantern frame, ₽60M 3 Lures, ₽100M a Kecleon Egg, ₽150M a shiny Togepi
- In-game Pokédex of 584 species: tracks every species seen and defeated; defeating a shiny, hatching an egg or playing a form catches it
- Daily and weekly missions (the same for everyone on the same day) and 63 achievements with bronze, silver and gold medals; some grant a title shown on the title and results screens. Some weekly missions and every gold medal also give an egg
- Map events that make you choose where to go: buff altars, healing fountains, locked chests guarded by an ambush, spike and bomb traps that hurt the horde too, and a fleeing Meowth that drops coins. Field missions pull the player across the map for ₽ and a level-up of rare cards: defend an egg in its nest from raiders, gather lost Poké Balls against the clock, or lead a lost Togepi to its nest
- Pokémon Mystery Dungeon-style pixel art (PMD SpriteCollab)
- Original chiptune soundtrack composed in code; Settings for music and effects volume, damage numbers, screen shake and language
- Touch controls with a floating joystick; installable as a fullscreen app

Good fit for people looking for: a Pokémon version of Vampire Survivors, a Pokémon roguelike or roguelite playable online, a free Pokémon browser game, a Pokémon game to play online with friends, or a Pokémon fan game for mobile without downloading.

## Guides and reference

- [Pokédex](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/pokedex/): every Pokémon in the game (588 species: the 27 starters and the 63 egg families, 90 playable lines in all, with their evolutions and branching forms, 415 wild species from every generation with their tier, bosses and legendaries, with how to catch each legendary for Legend Mode) with animated and shiny sprites, types, in-game stats, the moves each stage unlocks, Abilities, specials and when each one shows up. Portuguese: [Pokédex](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/pokedex/). Spanish: [Pokédex](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/pokedex/)
- Pokémon pages, one per playable Pokémon (the 27 starter lines, the 63 egg families, the 23 legendaries and the event legend Darkrai) at `/en/pokedex/<name>/`, e.g. [Charmander](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/pokedex/charmander/), [Eevee](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/pokedex/eevee/), [Gible](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/pokedex/gible/) and [Kyogre](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/pokedex/kyogre/): stats, evolutions (branches and items), starting move, learnset, Abilities, Mega Evolutions, and how to unlock or catch it. Portuguese at `/pokedex/<name>/`, Spanish at `/es/pokedex/<name>/`, French at `/fr/pokedex/<name>/`, Traditional Chinese at `/zh-tw/pokedex/<name>/`. The Pokédex links to all of them.
- [Tier list](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/tier-list/): the best Pokémon in Pokémon Survivors, ranked S to D from real players' runs (the last 30 days of finished runs, about 27,000, on Normal, Hard and Nightmare): each starter's and egg family's win rate against Mewtwo and average minute per difficulty, with the method (win rates smoothed toward each difficulty's average, difficulties weighed on an odds scale) and its caveats (beginners pick the famous starters, egg families are played by experienced players). Portuguese: [Tier list](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/tier-list/). Spanish: [Tier list](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/tier-list/)
- [How to play](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/guide/): controls (keyboard, gamepad, touch), how a run works, biomes and weather, the wild horde and its tiers, levels and moves (draft, forks, rare and shiny cards, Forget, TMs, Abilities and branching evolutions), move evolutions with held items, duo moves, cursed items, the special attack, types and status, boss timeline, special enemies, epic rifts and their domains, Legend Mode (how to catch each legendary, where it is beaten, wins needed, innate), shinies, map items, map events, the Kecleon Shop, missions and achievements, with the game's numbers. Portuguese: [Guia](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/guia/). Spanish: [Guía](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/guia/)
- [Changelog](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/changelog/): every update, newest first. Portuguese: [Novidades](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/novidades/). Spanish: [Novedades](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/novedades/)
- [Legal, privacy and credits](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/en/legal/): unofficial fan game, no ads or purchases, licenses, no personal data collected (localStorage only). Portuguese: [Legal](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/legal/). Spanish: [Legal](https://www.pokemonsurvivors.com/es/legal/)

## More

- [Community Discord server](https://discord.gg/Vx3RWFsjaD): English-speaking, with rooms for other languages; patch notes, the Daily Challenge podium and the daily outbreak are posted there. Players can link their game account to Discord to join, get their supporter role and a shiny Noibat as a Mystery Gift.
- [Official TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@pokemonsurvivors): @pokemonsurvivors, short clips of the game (gameplay, Mega Evolutions, new features).
- [Official YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@PokemonSurvivors): @PokemonSurvivors, the trailer, update videos and daily Shorts of the game.
- [Official Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/pokemonsurvivors/): @pokemonsurvivors, Reels and carousels of the game.
- [Source code and screenshots (GitHub)](https://github.com/pedrobarretto/pokemon-survivors)
- [Credits](https://github.com/pedrobarretto/pokemon-survivors/blob/main/CREDITS.md)
